rationale: Every `imports` target now carries a `resolvable` class, and before this none of the 263 emitted on the census draw did. `imports` is the only relationship type this analyzer emits whose target is not a symbol, so the type reported 0 % resolution and the store could not tell a target naming a file this corpus holds from a 404 — the round brief's cause C, measured in `validation/m14/fixtures/xml/imports-target-class.mts` (same draw `3bd539410d1a9189`: 0 of 263 marked before, 263 of 263 after, and the analyzer's class agrees with an independent filesystem walk on 263 of 263 — `external` 107, `file` 153, `in-document` 3, zero disagreements). The fixture pins all three classes on all THREE emitters, because each emitter is a separate `addRelationship` call and a marker added to two of them is a marker on two thirds of the type. `#local-style` is the `in-document` control and the only shape whose target could resolve to a symbol in the file it names; `/absolute/rooted.xsd` and `../shared/remote-style.xsl` are `file` controls at the two path extremes, and an absolute path being `file` rather than `external` is the assertion most likely to catch a scheme test that trips on the leading `/`. `https://example.invalid/remote.xsd` on `xs:import` is a FORBID row and not an oversight: `schemaLocation` already filters remote URIs before emitting (`isRemoteUri` at the call site), so `external` is unreachable from that emitter, and a fixture that asserted one would be asserting an edge the analyzer is right not to publish. `forbidRelationships` also pins that no edge from this document claims a class other than the three — the defect this feature could introduce is a fourth value, not a wrong one of three.

expectRelationships.note: DOCTYPE SYSTEM, relative path. The `file` class and NOT a claim that the file exists — the analyzer is a per-file unit and does no filesystem access.
A PI href naming a location in THIS file. The only `imports` shape whose target could bind to a symbol here.
Relative path with `..` in it. The class must be decided on the whole string, not on the first segment.
A PI href with a scheme. Same emitter as the two rows above, and a different class — the emitter is not what decides the class.
schemaLocation, ABSOLUTE. The leading `/` is what a naive scheme test reads as remote, so this row is the control on the control.

forbidRelationships.note: schemaLocation already drops remote URIs before emitting, so `external` is unreachable from that emitter. Asserting it here would demand an edge the analyzer is right not to publish — the same shape as a ruling whose overturn condition no correct implementation can meet.

The `namespace` half of a schemaLocation NAMESPACE/URI PAIR is a namespace name, not a path. Emitting it as an import target is the one shape this emitter could plausibly grow, and the first version of this fixture asserted it by forbidding every edge from `xs:import` — which the LOCAL `xs:import` legitimately produces, so the row could not be satisfied by a correct analyzer and was cut rather than weakened.

expectSymbols.name: xs:import
expectSymbols.note: the REMOTE `xs:import`. Its element and its `schemaLocation` attribute are still published even though no import edge comes of them — a fixture that only checked edges would pass on an analyzer that stopped publishing the element, which is a different and worse defect.
